intro.text: This is ComicToons. Your stream, inked live.
It turns Twitch stream moments into comic and manga pages that the streamer approves.

problem.text: A stream is great live, and then it vanishes.
The best moments scroll past in chat, and they are gone.
A viewer who joins halfway has no idea what just happened.
And a clip shows the video, but not what chat was saying.
So what if the night became a comic?

what-hero.text: ComicToons turns Twitch stream moments into comic pages.
The streamer connects their channel with their own Twitch app, or tries the built-in Sample, which needs no sign-in and no keys.

what-scroll.text: The best chat moments land on the overlay as panels, and the streamer approves every one.
When they log off, the whole night is a comic they can share.

arch.text: Here is how it works. Twitch provides chat over IRC, event notifications, and the live video.
arch.say: Here is how it works. Twitch provides chat over I R C, event notifications, and the live video.

arch.text: The server ingests those events. It removes duplicates, respects deletes and opt-outs, and caps the rate at sixty events a second.
Chat spikes, bursts of repeated emotes, and clusters of clips become candidate moments.
For each moment it captures real video frames with attributed chat. A page needs at least four distinct frames.
The page is composed as a source-frame comic, which needs no image key, or as an illustrated page from the provider you choose, with your own key.
arch.say: The page is composed as a source-frame comic, which needs no image key, or as an illustrated page from the provider you choose, with your own key.

arch.text: Speech balloons are lettered into reviewed pockets of the art, and they stay editable.
Then the streamer reviews every page, choosing Release, Reject, or Edit caption. Nothing airs unapproved.
Approved pages publish to the audience view, the OBS overlay, and a library of recaps, comic books and manga.
arch.say: Approved pages publish to the audience view, the O B S overlay, and a library of recaps, comic books and manga.

usecase.text: Let's follow a sample use case.
Critical Mess is a fictional tabletop night, streamed by juniper rolls. The built-in Sample needs no Twitch account and no keys. Going live does, as you will see.

connect.text: To go live, the streamer signs in with Twitch, using their own Twitch app. That also lets them read any public chat, read-only.
Tokens stay in the API server's memory.
connect.say: Tokens stay in the A P I server's memory.

keys.text: Going live needs your own keys. The built-in Sample needs none.
First, register your own Twitch app, and put its client ID and secret in a private environment file.
keys.say: First, register your own Twitch app, and put its client I D and secret in a private environment file.

keys.text: Then choose how pages are drawn. Source frames need no image key.
For illustrated pages, add your own key for OpenAI, Gemini, Pollinations or Cloudflare.
Keys live in your git-ignored environment file, never in the repository.

studio.text: Back in Sample mode, which needs no keys, pressing Run demo replays the fictional stream.
Panels release automatically as the scenes unfold, with live counters on top.
Chat is simulated locally, and every panel is labelled Sample, so nothing here pretends to be a real broadcast.
Twenty scenes later, the issue is ready to read.

viewers.text: The simulator lets you try a viewer joining, a raid, or a chat vote.
Each one shows up in the audience preview, on the same page.
A chat vote can pick the dialogue for a panel.

audience.text: The audience view shows released panels, with chat and votes one click away.
Catch-up gives late arrivals a quick recap.
And a viewer can join as a newcomer and take part.

catchup.text: Catch-up is a short Previously on card, with a five, fifteen, or thirty minute window.
So a late arrival is caught up in seconds.

library.text: The Library saves every issue and bundles the outputs.
Recap, comic book, manga series, and catch-up, each as a link or a PNG download.

recap.text: The recap shows every page at a glance, with PNG downloads.

book.text: The comic book reads cover to back page, two pages at a time.

manga.text: And the same story reads as a manga series, episode by episode.

overlay.text: For broadcast, the clean overlay is an OBS Browser Source, with no navigation.
overlay.say: For broadcast, the clean overlay is an O B S Browser Source, with no navigation.

overlay.text: Released panels, votes, and catch-up cards appear over the stream.
And Panic hide blanks the output instantly, if anything looks wrong.

tech.text: ComicToons is built with React and Vite on the front end, and Fastify on Node for the server.
It speaks Twitch OAuth, IRC chat and EventSub, supports four image providers with your own key, or none at all, and is tested with Playwright and axe-core.
tech.say: It speaks Twitch OAuth, I R C chat and EventSub, supports four image providers with your own key, or none at all, and is tested with Playwright and axe-core.

outro.text: Try the Sample demo, no keys needed, at comictoons-demo.vercel.app. Going live takes your own keys.
outro.say: Try the Sample demo, no keys needed, at comictoons dash demo, dot vercel, dot app. Going live takes your own keys.
